name: Western and Atlantic Railroad Tunnel
customer: Rail fans, Civil War readers, families
unique: The first major railroad tunnel in the South and the first bored through the Appalachian range, 1,477 feet long, with the original drill marks still in the rock and the spot where the Great Locomotive Chase passed in 1862.
buzz: Guided tours walk you into the bore with a flashlight and the guide tells the chase properly. Rail people call it the best railroad history stop in north Georgia.

name: The Huff House
customer: Civil War readers, house history people
unique: A Gothic revival house that faced the railroad until 1890, when the owner had it jacked onto a log turnstile and rotated by mule teams over two weeks to face the new street, with Johnston's headquarters and Cleburne's proposal inside its walls.
buzz: The house was turned around while the family lived in it, and that story alone justifies the visit. Tours are by appointment.

name: Dug Gap Battle Park
unique: Original Confederate earthworks and rock breastworks on the slope of Rocky Face Ridge, where the Atlanta Campaign opened and soldiers piled stone into the gaps between boulders.
buzz: You can walk the line and put a hand on the stacked rock, which most battlefields will not let you do. Quiet and easy to miss.

name: Chief Vann House State Historic Site
customer: History travellers, architecture people, Cherokee history readers
unique: A brick federal style mansion built by a Cherokee planter in 1804, with a floating staircase and hand carved mantels, preserved as the finest surviving building of the Cherokee Nation before removal.
buzz: The house is beautiful and the story of how the Vanns lost it is the part that lands. Guided tours explain the spiral staircase and the removal.

name: Fort Mountain State Park
unique: A mountaintop wall of stacked stone almost 900 feet long whose builders nobody can name, with a stone tower and a legend of a moon eyed people, plus a lake and ridge trails above the cloud line.
buzz: The wall is the reason people come and the debate about who built it has never been settled. The view west from the overlook is the other payoff.

name: Chatsworth Train Depot
unique: A restored depot in the middle of a small town that grew around the railroad, now the community event space, with the old platform and the tracks still in use behind it.
buzz: The town turns out here for festivals and the depot is the anchor. A natural stop on the way up to Fort Mountain.

name: New Echota State Historic Site
customer: History travellers, Cherokee history readers, school groups
unique: The capital of the Cherokee Nation before removal, reconstructed with the council house, the supreme court building and the print shop where the Cherokee Phoenix newspaper was set in Sequoyah's syllabary.
buzz: The print shop is the part people do not expect, a bilingual newspaper printed here in the 1820s. The site is quiet and the story is heavy.

name: Resaca Battlefield State Historic Site
unique: Preserved earthworks and a walking trail across the ground where the first big battle of the Atlanta Campaign was fought in May 1864, with the Union and Confederate lines still visible in the woods.
buzz: Recently preserved and lightly visited, with good interpretive signs and a loop that follows the trenches. Free and open at daylight.

name: Roland Hayes Museum at the Harris Arts Center
unique: The story of Roland Hayes, born to former slaves in Gordon County, who became the first Black American concert tenor to fill European halls, told with recordings and family material in the town arts center.
buzz: A remarkable life most visitors have never heard of, and the recordings make it real. Free and usually empty.

name: GEM Theatre
unique: A 1930s movie palace on Wall Street restored as a live venue, with the original marquee, a small balcony and a schedule of tribute acts, bluegrass and community theatre.
buzz: The room is small and the sound is good, and tickets stay under thirty dollars. It is the reason downtown Calhoun has an evening.

name: Chickamauga Battlefield
unique: The first national military park in the country, with a seven mile driving tour, hundreds of monuments and the Wilder Brigade tower, on ground where 34,000 men became casualties in two days.
buzz: Cyclists ride the loop on quiet roads and history people spend a whole day. The tower climb is worth the stairs.

name: Ringgold Depot
customer: Rail fans, Civil War readers, concert goers
unique: An 1849 stone depot that served as a hospital and a target during the war, still standing on the same tracks, now a performance hall where trains pass behind the stage.
buzz: The stone walls are original and the acoustics are better than they should be. Trains going by mid concert are part of the experience.

name: Lake Winnepesaukah
dates: May to September, weekends in spring and autumn
unique: A 1925 lakeside park with a wooden coaster from 1967, a boat ride that has run since the twenties and a picnic ground where families still bring coolers, minutes from the Tennessee line.
buzz: Generations of Chattanooga families learned to swim here. The Cannon Ball coaster is short and rough in the way people mean as a compliment.

name: Cloudland Canyon State Park
unique: A thousand foot deep sandstone gorge on Lookout Mountain with two waterfalls at the bottom of a staircase of several hundred steps, and rim trails that look across into three states.
buzz: The waterfall stairs are punishing and everyone says so. Go early, the rim overlooks fill at sunrise with photographers.

name: Dade County Courthouse and the End of the Chase
unique: A courthouse in the county where the Great Locomotive Chase ran out of track in 1862, with the local markers and the story of the Andrews Raiders strung out along the valley below Lookout Mountain.
buzz: The chase ended here and Dade County has never stopped telling it. Ask at the desk and someone will point you to the markers.

name: Howard Finster's Paradise Garden
customer: Outsider art people, music fans, families
unique: A Baptist preacher's four acre junk cathedral of concrete and mosaic, with towers, walkways and thousands of painted signs, built by Howard Finster, who painted album art for Talking Heads and R.E.M.
buzz: The gardens were nearly lost twice and volunteers pulled them back. Finster Fest in September brings the music crowd.

name: James H. Floyd State Park
unique: Two small lakes below Taylor Ridge with a trail that climbs to the remains of an old marble mine, campsites on the water and a swimming area in summer.
buzz: The marble mine trail is the unusual part and it is steep. The lakes are quiet and stocked.

name: Dub Denman Canoe Trail
unique: Twenty seven miles of the Tallapoosa River with three public launches, connecting to the Alabama Canoe Trail, on water locals call one of the cleanest runs in west Georgia.
buzz: Class I water for most of the run and quiet enough to see deer. Shuttle yourself, there is no outfitter on site.

name: Budapest Cemetery
unique: About twenty graves behind a stone arch, all that remains of a Hungarian wine making colony founded in 1888 that Prohibition killed by 1908.
buzz: A strange and sad little site in the middle of pine woods, with Hungarian names on the stones. Easy to miss without directions.

name: Bremen Depot Park
unique: A covered platform built to the design of the town's old depot with a scanner piped into the shelter, so you can listen to the dispatcher and know which of the forty daily trains is coming.
buzz: Kids love the scanner and the trains come close. A genuinely good twenty minute stop on I-20.

name: West Georgia Museum
unique: A recreated 1900s main street inside a museum, with a barber shop, a bank and a store you can walk into, plus a hall of dinosaur skeletons for the kids.
buzz: The mix of a period street and dinosaurs is odd and works. Cheap, indoors and good in the rain.

name: Silver Comet Trail
unique: A paved rail trail on the old Seaboard Air Line grade that runs from Smyrna to the Alabama line, with Cedartown as the western hub and long shaded cuts through the Piedmont.
buzz: The Cedartown trailhead has parking and a bike shop within reach. The grade is gentle enough for a whole family.

name: Big Spring Park
unique: A stone spring house over the water that the town was built around, in a shaded park a block from downtown Cedartown.
buzz: Small and cool and free, and the spring is still running. Good place to start a walk into town.

name: Museum of Coca-Cola Memorabilia
unique: Decades of Coca-Cola signs, trays, bottles and advertising in a small Cedartown collection, tracing how one Georgia company papered the country in red.
buzz: A niche collection in a small town, and free. Cola collectors make the trip from out of state.

name: The West Cinema
unique: An Art Deco movie house on Cedartown's main street, still showing films under a neon blade sign that lights the block after dark.
buzz: Cheap tickets, one screen and a lobby that smells like popcorn. The kind of theatre most towns have lost.
